title: Wasteland Renegades - free demo
author: KingofKingsofKingsof
selftext:
I'm reposting this as the video wasn't playing.  I have a free demo of my car combat game Wasteland Renegades on Itch.io.  You can play the first 2 levels in free run mode - survive as long as you can, and take down as many other cars as possible.  But manage your resources!  The full game is more or less ready (6 levels plus a bonus level, end of game boss, various locations), and I'm thinking about a Steam release (play's great on Steam Deck).  Any feedback would be much appreciated! I'm thinking of upping the difficulty.

[Wasteland Renegades: Warriors of the Road (Demo) by stuartking84](https://stuartking84.itch.io/wasteland-renegades)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
This is fckn tight. 

First thing I'll say is that the most important part of the experience - the kinetic feeling of the impacts and the driving - is bang-on. This is the only action or driving-oriented game I've played from this sub where I genuinely got into a flow state and was really feeling the play. 

The foundation for an excellent experience is solid. 

My critiques: 

 \- This is very nitpicky, but the default keybindings are just bad. F to fire, really? It signals to the player that it is a game made by someone who doesn't play on PC. WASD would movement be the standard, it's more ergonomically friendly than the arrow keys especially for laptop keyboards, Space is fine for boost, probably enter or backspace to shoot. Things like 'F to Fire' is a relic of bad Capcom ports. We can leave that past behind us. 

 \- There are moments in the game that feel like they should be unrecoverable but aren't. I feel like if the player goes off of the road and hits a hazard, that should be an instant game over. Hitting sand should probably deplete health or something; it slows the action, which feels like it should come with a meaningful penalty. 

 \- The way the pick-ups from enemies work is pure genius... I am not sold on the fungible ammunition resource, though. I think it would be more fun if weapons were specific things the player could pick up, with their own ammo finite counters. So the machine gun can stay in, but it's has \[X\] bullets and then it's done, but there could be missiles or a vehicular bolas or a big mechanical saw that extends from the side of the car or etc etc etc. Having a just a machine gun with limited ammo, IMHO, makes the ammo pick-ups fall too heavily on the side of 'pay tax to have fun' rather than filling-up a weapon system. 

 \- I think the fuel resource would be interesting as a secondary health resource as well as the boost resource. I didn't feel like I was really trying to manage my fuel, just picking it up to soend it down. And it makes sense that if the car is out of gas, the ride's over. 

 \- The most fun and hilarious moments in the game are when there is a big cluster of cars on the road; I feel like that could really be leaned into. At the moment, enemy cars can't interact with each other very much - I think it would be more fun if they could, so a clever boost or clever weapon use could cause a massive pile-up / chain reaction. 

 \- ...Depending on how splattery you want to get, this feels like the kind of game begging for things like people flying out of the cars and getting gibbed / run over on the road. Or things like cars being catapulted right into the camera, causing momentary cracks in the lens like in some old arcade games. 

 \- I feel like just a little bit of telegraphing from all attacks would improve the experience slightly, like how the gunner popping-up telegraphs the shooting. Maybe not enough to even fairly warn the player - just enough so they FEEL like being hit by an attack was their mistake. Lots of times I drove into the dynamite and didn't know how to feel about it - if there had been a guy tossing the dynamite, even just a couple of frames of him doing it, I'd have thought, "Oh, that was stupid of me, should've seen that coming". Creating that sense of skill expression even if some of it is illusory. 

  
Great job. I hope this project matures into something.

replies.author: KingofKingsofKingsof
replies.body:
thanks for the feedback.  I'll definitely have a think about that.  

Agreed on the controls - I focused mainly on controller and touch screen, so keys needs improving.  

I like the idea about the splattering and people.  Something I'd like to try is having people jump onto your car, and also people in the road.  

I did consider fuel as a 'timer', but thought the game might be too hard, especially since health serves a similar purpose.  I thought having it affect your boost gives you a 'weapon' to manage.  However, as I've got better as the game, I now find it too easy, so maybe there is something to that...  

As for weapons, I hadn't thought of having a 'one and done' type approach - it would change the end game which can be beaten fairly easily if you manage to get loads of bullets saved up, so actually a limited set of ammo might make it more of a challenge and force you to think about your next pickup, and give the added bonus to have other weapon types. Thanks!

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Yeah, I definitely found myself hoarding bullets, which could be a problem for boss fights. 

If the weapons were instead one-and-done power-ups, it would address hoarding and also be something a hypothetical boss fight could lean into. Like, the boss occasionally produces a power-up, and driving over it becomes part of the rhythm/strategy for beating the boss.
